cards.alt: Sample multiple choice card: Side-chain charge of Asp at pH 7.4?

questions.stem: What is the approximate net charge of the tripeptide Lys-Asp-Gly at pH 7.4?
questions.explanation: At pH 7.4 the free N-terminal amine is +1, the Lys side chain is +1, the Asp side chain is -1, and the free C-terminal carboxylate is -1, for a net charge of 0. Answering +1 or +2 forgets one or both negative groups, and -1 forgets the N-terminus.
questions.subtopic: Side chain pKa values and charge at physiological pH

questions.stem: Why does the peptide bond not rotate freely?
options: Resonance gives the C-N bond partial double bond character
questions.explanation: Delocalization of the nitrogen lone pair onto oxygen makes the amide plane rigid. A hydrogen bond, ionic bond, or disulfide would be a different type of interaction and would not describe the amide linkage.
questions.subtopic: Peptide bond formation, resonance and hydrolysis

questions.stem: An enzyme transfers an amino group from one molecule to another. Which EC class?
questions.explanation: Group transfer defines EC 2 (transferases), as with aminotransferases. Ligases join molecules using ATP, lyases cleave without water or redox, and isomerases rearrange one molecule.

options: Covalently acetylating a serine in the active site
questions.explanation: Aspirin transfers an acetyl group to a Ser, permanently blocking the enzyme. Reversible competitors (such as ibuprofen) behave differently, and aspirin does not target ES or heme.

questions.stem: Iron in the heme of hemoglobin must be in which state to bind oxygen?
questions.explanation: Fe2+ (ferrous) binds O2 reversibly. Fe3+ (methemoglobin) does not bind oxygen, and Fe0 and Fe4+ are not the physiological states in heme.
questions.subtopic: Conjugated proteins, prosthetic groups and glycoproteins
